action_criteria.expected_evidence: Evans index 0.34 with DESH, an acute callosal angle (82 degrees) and enlarged temporal horns (MTA 1); chronic left precentral and corona radiata infarct with no new infarct; Fazekas grade 2; patent aqueduct; no obstructing lesion
action_criteria.label: Brain MRI for ventricular size, iNPH supportive features, new ischaemia and an obstructing cause
action_criteria.rationale: A new decline on top of a stable post-stroke baseline needs an MRI that separates new infarction from ventriculomegaly and excludes obstruction before CSF is removed.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Normal blood count, electrolytes, creatinine 1.0 mg/dL, glucose, INR, TSH and vitamin B12; RPR and HIV non-reactive
action_criteria.label: Targeted labs for reversible contributors and LP safety
action_criteria.rationale: Renal function and the blood count matter for the apixaban hold and the tap, and a thyroid and B12 screen is reasonable, but none decides the iNPH question.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: TUG 32 s, 10-metre walk 26 s in 34 steps, 180-degree turn in 8 steps, start hesitation and en-bloc turning with a mild right circumduction
action_criteria.label: Baseline timed gait assessment before the tap
action_criteria.rationale: Two falls and a mixed gait (new bilateral shuffling on a right spastic circumduction) need an objective baseline before the tap.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: MoCA 20/30 with executive, attention, fluency and free-recall deficits, recall improving with cues
action_criteria.label: Bedside cognitive screen
action_criteria.rationale: His son reports a marked memory and processing decline, so a MoCA documents the profile and the tap baseline.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Opening pressure 15 cmH2O, normal cells, protein and glucose; 40 mL removed; TUG 32 to 28 s at 2 hours and 26.5 s at 24 hours (17%), 10-metre walk 26 to 21 s, MoCA unchanged at 20
action_criteria.label: Lumbar tap test with opening pressure and CSF removal
action_criteria.rationale: Normal-pressure CSF and an objective response separate the iNPH component from fixed vascular deficits and predict shunt benefit.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: TUG 28 s at 2 hours and 26.5 s at 24 hours (17% faster); 10-metre walk 21 s at 24 hours (19% faster); circumduction and MoCA unchanged
action_criteria.label: Post-tap timed gait reassessment
action_criteria.rationale: Repeating the same timed measures at 2 and 24 hours shows which part of his gait responds and which (the post-stroke circumduction) does not.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not perform the large-volume lumbar tap before brain MRI has excluded a mass or obstructive hydrocephalus

Do not diagnose iNPH from ventriculomegaly alone: the diagnosis needs the clinical syndrome (gait disturbance with cognitive or urinary symptoms) and supportive imaging, with no other cause explaining them [Relkin_2005]
Do not perform the lumbar tap while apixaban is active and do not bridge with heparin [ASRA_2025] [ACCP_2022]
Do not attribute the new gait and cognitive decline to the old stroke or small-vessel disease alone once ventriculomegaly with DESH and a tap response are documented
Do not attribute the syndrome to normal ageing or deconditioning once the ventriculomegaly and the tap response are documented
required_recommendations: Refer to neurosurgery for CSF shunting with a programmable valve, on the basis of the tap-test improvement of 17% in TUG at 24 hours, the DESH MRI and normal-pressure CSF [Nakajima_2021]

Hold apixaban for at least 72 hours before the lumbar tap and restart it no sooner than 24 hours after, without heparin bridging, weighing the interruption against the stroke risk of atrial fibrillation (CHA2DS2-VASc 4, prior stroke) [ASRA_2025] [ACCP_2022]
Falls-prevention measures (physiotherapy, home assessment, walking aid) while awaiting surgery
Counsel that shunting is expected to improve the new shuffling gait and urinary urgency, not the fixed post-stroke right-sided weakness and circumduction

avoided_actions.rationale: He has no episodes suggesting seizures after the old infarct, so an EEG cannot separate iNPH from its mimics.
His paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is already known and anticoagulated, and the falls are not syncopal, so an ECG does not inform the gait work-up.
The stroke was 5 years ago with a known cardioembolic source already treated, so echocardiography does not change this work-up.
An MRI is available and shows DESH, the callosal angle, the old infarct and the absence of new ischaemia better than CT.
Atrial fibrillation is already documented and anticoagulated, so rhythm monitoring adds nothing to the gait work-up.
Molecular or advanced imaging does not change the iNPH decision, which rests on MRI and the tap test
A full neuropsychological battery is not needed for the iNPH decision; the bedside screen and timed gait measures are
Normal-pressure CSF with a normal cell count in a chronic afebrile gait syndrome gives no indication for prion, inflammatory or infectious assays.

differential.diagnosis: Vascular cognitive impairment / progressive small-vessel ischaemic disease
differential.key_features: The old left infarct and Fazekas grade 2 white matter change contribute to his deficits, but a stable post-stroke course for years followed by new bilateral shuffling, DESH, ventricles out of proportion to the white matter burden and a 17% TUG response make iNPH the cause of the new decline.
Bilateral leg tone increase without rest tremor or upper-limb bradykinesia, and a gait that improved after CSF removal, argue against parkinsonism.
Executive and attention deficits with cued recall, hippocampi of MTA 1 and a gait-first course do not suggest Alzheimer's disease as the main cause.

differential.diagnosis: Cerebral atrophy with secondary ex-vacuo ventriculomegaly
differential.key_features: DESH with tight convexity sulci, an acute callosal angle and a tap response argue against atrophy ex vacuo.
The old stroke was ischaemic, without haemorrhage, and there is no history of head trauma, meningitis or intracranial surgery.

key_clinical_evidence: A gait that had been stable at its post-stroke level for years worsened over 10 to 12 months with bilateral shuffling and start hesitation, urinary urgency and memory decline, without a new infarct on MRI, which meets the clinical criteria for probable iNPH [Relkin_2005]
MRI shows Evans index 0.34 with DESH (tight convexity sulci and enlarged Sylvian fissures), an acute callosal angle (82 degrees) and a patent aqueduct [Nakajima_2021]

Opening pressure 15 cmH2O with normal CSF content; after 40 mL was removed, TUG improved 17% at 24 hours (32 to 26.5 s) and the 10-metre walk 19%, while the right circumduction and MoCA did not change [Nakajima_2021]
Tap-test sensitivity is 26% to 61% with a PPV of 73% to 100%; the positive tap supports shunting [Marmarou_2005]
The old infarct and Fazekas grade 2 white matter change make a vascular contribution certain but do not preclude a shunt response [Tisell_2011]
Apixaban for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation with a prior stroke (CHA2DS2-VASc 4) must be held for at least 72 hours before the neuraxial puncture without heparin bridging [ASRA_2025] [ACCP_2022]

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: The post-stroke deficits had been stable for years; a new bilateral shuffling gait with start hesitation, urinary urgency and memory decline, with DESH and a tap response, points to superimposed iNPH rather than progression of vascular disease alone.
red_herrings.data_point: Remote ischemic stroke (left MCA territory, 5 years ago, with mild residual right hand weakness)
red_herrings.intended_effect: New gait decline is attributed to progressive vascular cognitive impairment alone

sequence_constraints.reason: Brain imaging must exclude a mass or obstructive hydrocephalus before CSF is removed [Relkin_2005]
The baseline gait must be measured before the tap, or the post-tap change cannot be interpreted [Nakajima_2021]
The timed gait is repeated after the tap, at 2 to 24 hours, so that its change from the baseline measures the response to CSF removal [Nakajima_2021]

patient.chief_complaint: Worsening walking difficulties, memory decline and urinary urgency on top of a prior stroke

past_medical_history: Remote ischemic stroke (left MCA territory, 5 years ago, with mild residual right hand weakness)

patient.history_present_illness: A 72-year-old right-handed Hispanic man with hypertension, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on apixaban, and a remote left MCA ischemic stroke 5 years ago (with mild residual right hand weakness that has been stable since 6 months post-stroke) was admitted for evaluation of a new decline in gait and cognition. He and his son report that over approximately 10-12 months, he has developed new symptoms on top of his post-stroke baseline: his gait, which had been stable at his post-stroke level for years, has significantly worsened with shuffling quality, wide base, and difficulty initiating movement. He has had two falls at home in the past 4 months. His son notes he is far more forgetful and slowed in thinking than he was 18 months ago. He now needs assistance managing his medications. Additionally, he has developed urinary urgency with two episodes of incontinence per week. His outpatient neurologist initially attributed the gait decline to evolving small vessel disease from his prior stroke history, but a repeat MRI obtained 2 months ago at an outside facility was reported as showing enlarged ventricles; the images are not available, and he was referred for further evaluation.
